- Rising costs, supply disruptions, and import restrictions on essential raw materials may impact our expenses, timelines, and overall financial performance.
- The prices of our primary raw materials, including those imported for the production of Adhesive Tapes, Polishing and Buffing Pads, Rubbing and Polishing Compounds have been volatile.
- We source raw materials such as Jumbo Rolls, Solvents, Skins, Heat Film and Velcro for our manufacturing operations from a combination of domestic and foreign suppliers.
- Raw materials used in the manufacturing of Adhesive Tapes, Rubbing and Polishing Compounds, and Buffing Pads are global commodities, and their prices tend to be cyclical, fluctuating in response to global market conditions.
- Our raw materials are imported from China, Japan, Portugal, Taiwan, United States of America, Spain, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Germany, Malaysia and Turkey.
- If the costs of these raw materials rise due to factors such as rise in input and commodity prices or shortages in supply, and our Company is not able to recover these costs through cost saving measures elsewhere or by increasing the prices of its products, our results of operations could be adversely affected.
- In the event prices for these raw materials subsequently decline there can be no assurance that our Company will be able to price our products based on the material costs it actually incurred.
- Our Registered Office and Manufacturing unit from where we operate is not owned by us.

verdict.our_read: Sumax Engineering Limited is a 1994-incorporated, Secunderabad-headquartered converter and trader of automotive adhesive tapes and die-cuts, pre-taped masking film, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing and foam pads, domes and graphics and car-care products, with a bought-in trading line of tools, abrasives, body-shop consumables and aerosols, made at two units at SIPCOT Sriperumbudur (Tamil Nadu) and IMT Manesar (Haryana) under ISO 9001:2015, IATF 16949:2016, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018. All figures in the DRHP are printed '(Rs In Lakhs)'. Scale is small: revenue from operations of ₹12,682.09, ₹13,079.45 and ₹14,612.60 lakhs in FY23, FY24 and FY25 (FY25 = ₹146.13 crore) and ₹7,174.69 lakhs in H1FY26, with EBITDA margin climbing 6.32% to 8.84% to 10.21% to 11.80% and restated PAT of ₹464.44, ₹744.02, ₹999.32 and ₹580.02 lakhs (FY25 PAT = ₹9.99 crore). The revenue base is undiversified by end-market — the DRHP states sales to Automotive Industry suppliers were 100% in each of FY23, FY24, FY25 and the period ended September 30, 2025 — with top-10 customers at 44.35%, 43.92%, 46.43% and 52.67% and no firm-commitment agreements with any of them, and adhesive tapes and die-cuts at 45.00% of the H1FY26 mix. Inputs are the mirror image: raw material consumed was 47.10%, 44.29%, 43.26% and 37.01% of total revenues, and Annexure XLIII shows the imported share of consumption rising 65.97% / 65.45% / 66.20% / 84.92%, sourced across twelve countries, with foreign-currency expenditure of ₹3,727.99 lakhs in H1FY26 alone. Returns look high on a thin asset base (RoCE 19.70% / 23.32% / 24.63%, RoNW 14.75% / 19.11% / 20.42%, net fixed assets of only ₹698.13 lakhs against FY25 revenue), but FY25 cash flow from operations was ₹69.98 lakhs against that ₹999.32 lakh PAT, after an inventory build of ₹590.56 lakhs, a receivables build of ₹418.48 lakhs and income tax paid of ₹361.77 lakhs. The Offer is up to 53,00,000 Equity Shares of ₹10 — a Fresh Issue of up to 43,00,000 shares on a pre-Offer base of 1,47,31,500 shares, plus an Offer for Sale of up to 10,00,000 shares entirely by Mr. Sudeep Mehta (9,00,000) and Mrs. Vimla Mehta (1,00,000), whose proceeds go to them and not to the Company, and an employee reservation of up to 2,10,000 shares — on NSE Emerge. Identified Fresh Issue objects total ₹3,351.02 lakhs by my addition: ₹488.68 lakhs of building at a proposed Unit I at Tapukara, Rajasthan, ₹1,662.34 lakhs of building at a proposed Unit II at MET Jhajjar, Haryana, and ₹1,200.00 lakhs of working capital in FY2026-27, with general corporate purposes, the Offer Price, post-Issue capital and every P/E cell printed as placeholders. Land for both units (₹957.00 and ₹1,329.56 lakhs, ₹2,286.56 lakhs by my addition) is stated as already acquired and incurred with Nil IPO funding, while the DRHP also states no amount had been deployed towards the objects till September 30, 2025 — a date at which net fixed assets stood at ₹760.63 lakhs. Ownership is 100% Promoter and Promoter Group across 7 shareholders, with the entire 38,10,000-share Minimum Promoter's Contribution coming from a 6:1 bonus allotted on March 11, 2026, nineteen days before this March 30, 2026 filing, for consideration other than cash; the securities premium account before the Issue is Nil; and the issuer states twice that it has no comparable listed peers in India, so the document carries no peer P/E, no peer accounting-ratio comparison and no market-share figure.

parameter_scores.basis: 31 years of operation since December 21, 1994, IATF 16949:2016 plus ISO 9001/14001/45001, stated OEM Best Supplier and Best Customer Support awards (2019), collaborations recorded with a Portugal-based company (2004) and a Japanese company (2013), and a claim to be among the few with in-line doming application units. Against that, the DRHP discloses no market share and no competitive rank, describes its market only as having 'limited numbers of operators', states twice that there are no comparable listed peers in India, and confirms it holds no firm-commitment agreements with customers. Adhesive tapes and die-cuts are 45.00% of the H1FY26 mix, while traded lines (abrasives 24.12%, tools 1.69%, body-shop consumables 1.78%, retail 0.04%, aerosols 0.09%) are 27.72% of H1FY26 revenue by my addition of the printed line percentages, so a material part of what is sold is resold rather than made.

Revenue from operations ₹12,682.09 to ₹13,079.45 to ₹14,612.60 lakhs, printed growth of 35.18% (FY23), 3.13% (FY24) and 11.72% (FY25) — a two-year CAGR of 7.3% by my arithmetic — with H1FY26 at ₹7,174.69 lakhs. Absolute scale is small at ₹146.13 crore of FY25 revenue. Growth is uneven at the line level: Rubbing and Polishing Compounds fell ₹1,605.05 to ₹1,321.84 lakhs and Reflective Tapes ₹98.38 to ₹12.32 lakhs FY23-FY25, while traded Abrasive Sheets rose ₹2,421.08 to ₹2,913.54 lakhs and Car Care Products ₹283.72 to ₹655.71 lakhs. The KPI table prints 'NA' for H1FY26 revenue growth.

EBITDA rose ₹804.77 to ₹1,162.57 to ₹1,503.41 lakhs with margin 6.32% to 8.84% to 10.21%, and H1FY26 EBITDA of ₹855.31 lakhs at 11.80%; PAT margin 3.66% to 5.69% to 6.84% to 8.08%. Raw material consumed dropped from 47.10% to 37.01% of total revenues over the same span, finance cost fell ₹62.86 to ₹60.82 to ₹56.75 lakhs, and depreciation stayed modest at ₹90.64 to ₹106.02 to ₹107.99 lakhs. Marked down from higher because part of the step carries non-recurring support: FX translation gains of ₹91.03 lakhs in FY25 (9.1% of PAT by my arithmetic) and ₹23.54 lakhs in H1FY26, plus H1FY26 discount received of ₹29.82 lakhs against ₹0.76 lakhs for all of FY25.

Of ₹105.72 lakhs of FY25 other income, ₹91.03 lakhs is FX translation gain and ₹7.71 lakhs profit on sale of investments, both classified Non-Recurring by the DRHP's own annexure; of ₹70.84 lakhs in H1FY26, ₹29.82 lakhs is discount received (labelled 'not related to business activity'), ₹23.54 lakhs FX, ₹8.60 lakhs investment profit and ₹7.45 lakhs liabilities written back. The restatement reverses direction in the stub: audited PAT of ₹526.02 lakhs becomes ₹580.02 lakhs restated, +₹54.00 lakhs by my subtraction, on a Prior Period Income/Expense line of ₹105.92 lakhs equal to 18.3% of the restated half-year PAT by my arithmetic, against downward restatements of ₹34.76, ₹10.86 and ₹10.68 lakhs (my subtractions) in FY23, FY24 and FY25. The reconciliation notes list depreciation useful-life errors, gratuity and leave encashment recognised outside AS 15, rent outside AS 19, and eight expense heads recognised in the wrong year.

FY25 CFO of ₹69.98 lakhs against restated PAT of ₹999.32 lakhs is 7.0% conversion by my arithmetic; cumulative FY23-FY25 CFO of ₹779.93 lakhs against cumulative PAT of ₹2,207.78 lakhs is 35.3%, both totals my addition. FY25 absorbed ₹590.56 lakhs into inventory and ₹418.48 lakhs into receivables and paid ₹361.77 lakhs of tax. Held back by liquidity at the reporting date: cash of ₹35.96 lakhs (closing cash ₹22.56 lakhs) versus ₹571.80 lakhs at March 31, 2025, sanctioned working-capital facilities of only ₹860.00 lakhs against restated working capital of ₹4,698.30 lakhs, and ₹2,286.56 lakhs of land for the two proposed units (my addition of ₹957.00 and ₹1,329.56 lakhs) stated as already incurred with Nil IPO funding while the DRHP also states nothing had been deployed towards the objects till September 30, 2025, when net fixed assets were ₹760.63 lakhs. risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Rising costs, supply disruptions, and import restrictions on essential raw materials may impact our expenses, timelines, and overall financial performance.
- The prices of our primary raw materials, including those imported for the production of Adhesive Tapes, Polishing and Buffing Pads, Rubbing and Polishing Compounds have been volatile.
- We source raw materials such as Jumbo Rolls, Solvents, Skins, Heat Film and Velcro for our manufacturing operations from a combination of domestic and foreign suppliers.
- Raw materials used in the manufacturing of Adhesive Tapes, Rubbing and Polishing Compounds, and Buffing Pads are global commodities, and their prices tend to be cyclical, fluctuating in response to global market conditions.
- Our raw materials are imported from China, Japan, Portugal, Taiwan, United States of America, Spain, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Germany, Malaysia and Turkey.
- If the costs of these raw materials rise due to factors such as rise in input and commodity prices or shortages in supply, and our Company is not able to recover these costs through cost saving measures elsewhere or by increasing the prices of its products, our results of operations could be adversely affected.
- In the event prices for these raw materials subsequently decline there can be no assurance that our Company will be able to price our products based on the material costs it actually incurred.
- Our Registered Office and Manufacturing unit from where we operate is not owned by us.
